featured_reviews.review_text: I had few cats neutered with this NGO. Good thing is that they are good at surgery. Bad thing. The staff never picks up call or responds to your concerns about the cat. As a caretaker, we are concerned for our cats health especially if they are at a new place. As an NGO they should understand and inculcate in this behaviour. Swapna is too rude and arrogant. She should improve her behaviour and talking skills with people. You are not doing any favour on your customers. In facts customer favours you. This attitude won’t go long way. However she’s compassionate towards animals. As a lawyer, I understand the challenges faced by an NGO, but it never provides you a leeway to behave badly.

featured_reviews.name: Mohsin Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I took my cat, Panda, to All About Them for neutering. She was a tuxedo cat. I was charged ₹2,500 for the procedure, which included post-operative care. However, when I brought her home after she stayed at their clinic for two days following the surgery, she seemed extremely lethargic.

Fifteen days after bringing her back, she suddenly fell very ill and had difficulty walking. I rushed her to the hospital, where the vet mentioned that she might have contracted a viral infection from being in a place with many other cats. When I informed the doctor that she had been neutered and had stayed at All About Them for two days, he confirmed that it was possible she had picked up the infection there.

Unfortunately, despite receiving multiple injections and fluids, she couldn’t recover and sadly passed away the same day. I don’t directly blame All About Them, but I am deeply disappointed because they assured me that the cats would be well cared for during post-op recovery. Had I known that infections were a risk at their facility, I would have taken her home immediately after the surgery instead.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had a very terrible experience at this hospital. The staff is unsupportive and they seemed indifferent to my concern. I went there for my cat, he had jaundice. They said there is no space for him. They work on first come first serve basis, the doctors said he has no rights to decide if your cat will get addmission here or not, only the ward attendant will decide that. featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

featured_reviews.review_text: Worst place ever. Don't ever take your street dog or pet dog here. Here I am sharing my own experience. owner_posts.post_text:
Behind every healthy smile of our child is a doctor’s dedication, care, and kindness. 💙

This International Doctor’s Day, we celebrate the incredible professionals who stand beside our children with patience, expertise, and compassion.

From tiny moments of care to life-changing support, your presence helps our children feel safe, strong, and cared for.

Thank you for being a part of their journey✨

Learning through Role play! 🌟

Our children enjoyed an engaging Role Play Session conducted by Morgann stanely volunteers. Through fun scenarios like patient–doctor, teacher–student, and more, children explored different roles, practiced communication, and learned how to respond in various situations.

A fun-filled activity that encouraged confidence and social skills in children ✨

Our children enjoyed a wonderful and engaging storytelling session✨

Through interactive stories, the children explored important values, enhanced their listening and imagination skills, and actively participated by sharing their thoughts and experiences. Their enthusiasm, curiosity, and involvement made the session truly special.

A heartfelt thank you to   volunteers from Giant Group of Byculla for creating a fun learning experience that inspired our young minds.

Our children had fun creating cute paper puppy puppets with colours, folding, and with their creativity. ✂️✨

Such activities boost creativity and help to build focus and confidence. 🌟

At Bal Asha Trust, we believe every child’s rightful place is in a family. 💛

This belief continues to guide our work in family restoration, reunification, and adoption because children thrive best with love, belonging, and emotional security.

Last year alone, 115 children were connected to families through our efforts, including 101 family restorations and 14 adoptions. ❤️

On the International Day of Families, we reaffirm our commitment to ensuring that every child has the opportunity to grow up with the warmth, care, and support of family life.

We are happy to felicitate our 10 SSC students from our Education sponsorship programme who have passed their Board exams.

Their dedication has made us proud ✨

Where play meets purpose and learning feels like fun. 

Kids learning about vehicles 🚗

Such interactive activities help our children develop skills, curiosity, and a love for learning.

It was an honour for Bal Asha Trust to be chosen to share our experiences with government officials from Tamil Nadu, who visited to gain insights into the functioning of a Specialised Adoption Agency (SAA) and child protection practices followed in Mumbai.

As part of a DWCD training organized by TISS,  The officials undertook field visits to understand on-ground child protection systems in Maharashtra, and we were grateful to be among the organisations they chose to learn from.

Such knowledge-sharing visits strengthen collective efforts toward building safer and more responsive child protection systems for children. 🤝💙

Before support begins, clarity comes first. 💛

At Bal Asha Trust, our social workers engage closely with families even before enrolment into the Education Sponsorship Programme. Through orientation sessions, they help families understand the purpose of the programme, eligibility criteria, and how children will be supported.

This year, we are focusing on deeper engagement with families and scaling our reach, so that more children can benefit from the right support at the right time. 🤝📖

Because when expectations are aligned, support becomes truly meaningful.

featured_reviews.name: D Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Heartfelt Thank You to TATF & Deepa

As many of our friends know, 2023 didn’t end gently for us. It was a time filled with grief, long days, and sleepless nights.

But in that silence, we realized we might need someone to help us through.

Not something impulsive, not a rushed decision, just an unspoken understanding between the two of us that perhaps the love we had to give wasn’t meant to stop.

And that’s when fate stepped in.

While scrolling through Instagram one night, I came across The Anubis-Tiger Foundation. Something nudged me to send a message, just putting it out there that we were open to welcoming a pup in need of a home.

I didn’t expect a reply so soon. But within a few hours, Deepa reached out - with a photo of an angel who, as it turned out, was waiting for us too.

The moment we saw her, we just knew.
She was ours. And we were hers.

Despite everything, I never imagined it would all happen so quickly. But perhaps that’s because I hadn’t realized just how many people are out there giving up their pets, sometimes for heartbreaking reasons. It left me sad, confused, and questioning how anyone could let go of such love.

But I’ll be honest - we’re also thankful.

Because if that family hadn’t made their decision, we would’ve never met Aura.

On 21st January 2024, we brought her home. We braced ourselves, thinking she might take time to adjust after a year with her previous family.

But Aura had other plans.

Within a day, she chose us - just as we had chosen her. She knew she was home.

She changed everything. The energy, the silence, the air itself. And her name came so naturally: Aura.

We went into this thinking we were rescuing her. But in truth, she rescued us.

We are so grateful to have her in our lives.

Thank you, Deepa, you who don’t just find homes for these beautiful souls, but make sure they find the right ones.

She doesn’t hand them over to just anyone. She takes the time to check, to understand, and to ensure that the home is one filled with the love, care, and stability every animal deserves.

Thank you, Anubis Foundation.
And thank you to the angel above who showed us the way.

❤️
